units.title: PIVD: Disc Anatomy
units.guide: PIVD is a protrusion of the disc compressing the cord or nerves, most often at L4-L5, then L5-S1. Remember the jelly nucleus (type II collagen) wrapped in the tough fibrous annulus (type I collagen).

units.title: PIVD: Mechanism & Degeneration Steps
units.guide: Abnormal loading and degeneration of the spine set the stage for a four-step cascade: degeneration → prolapse (bulging nucleus pulposus) → extrusion (AF breaks, NP comes out) → sequestration (extruded NP breaks away).

units.title: Canal Stenosis: Causes & Contrast
units.guide: Canal stenosis comes from PIVD or from excessive abnormal bone growth of vertebral degeneration in OA, most often in the lumbar region. Contrast it with PIVD: stenosis is elderly and chronic, PIVD is young and acute.

units.title: PIVD: Types & Nerve Injured
units.guide: Far lateral prolapse hits the exiting nerve root, while the common paracentral type impinges the traversing root. The most commonly injured nerve is L5, giving a lower motor neuron lesion picture.

units.title: PIVD: Clinical Features
units.guide: Think heavy lifting history, low back ache and sciatica — back pain radiating to the lower limb that worsens with flexion, sneezing, coughing and prolonged sitting. PIVD is the most common cause of sciatica.

units.title: PIVD: Evaluation
units.guide: SLRT is positive when the hip cannot flex beyond 30-35° because raising the leg stretches the compressed nerve and produces pain. MRI is the IOC, and the neurological exam localizes the lesion by the nerve roots involved.

units.title: Myotomes & Reflexes
units.guide: Climb the myotome ladder: C5 elbow flexion, C6 wrist extension, C7 elbow extension & wrist flexion, C8 finger flexion, T1 finger abduction, then L2 hip flexion, L3 knee extension, L4 ankle dorsiflexion, L5 toe extension, S1 ankle plantar flexion. Reflexes: C5 biceps, C6 supinator, C7 triceps, L3-4 knee, S1 ankle.

units.title: PIVD: Conservative Treatment
units.guide: Conservative care is simple: rest in semi-fowler position (supine with 30-40° flexion of spine) plus physiotherapy.

units.title: PIVD: Surgical Treatment
units.guide: Operate with total/hemi-laminectomy or laminotomy + discectomy when symptoms worsen despite conservative Rx, bowel & bladder are involved, a massive central prolapse compresses multiple roots, or cauda equina syndrome develops.

units.title: Conus Medullaris vs Cauda Equina
units.sec: Conus medullaris v/s cauda equina syndrome · p183
units.guide: Conus (spinal cord, nucleus of Onuf S2; injury at L1) gives UMNL with LMNL features, symmetric areflexic flaccid paralysis and a normal knee reflex. Cauda (spinal nerves; large disc below L1) gives asymmetric LMNL with lost knee reflex. Both share saddle anaesthesia, bowel & bladder involvement and a lost ankle reflex.

units.title: Lumbar Canal Stenosis: Pathophysiology
units.guide: LCS runs a straight line: spondylosis (OA of facet joints) → excessive bone formation → stenosis of the lumbar canal → neurogenic claudication.

units.title: LCS: Claudication Patterns
units.guide: LCS pain eases with flexion (sitting, leaning over, climbing upstairs) and worsens with extension (walking, standing upright). Neurogenic claudication starts in the back, is caused by standing and relieved by climbing stairs, with postural changes and normal pulses; vascular starts in the calf, is relieved by standing, caused by climbing, and has abnormal pulses.

units.title: LCS vs PIVD
units.guide: LCS: elderly, slow & progressive onset, pain decreases on flexion. PIVD: young, acute onset, pain increases on flexion.

units.title: Spondylolisthesis: Definition & Cause
units.guide: Spondylolisthesis is slipping of one vertebra over another, caused by trauma/fracture of the pars interarticularis.

units.title: Spondylolisthesis: Radiology
units.guide: On the scottie dog: spondylolisthesis loses its head (beheaded scottish terrier, m/c L5-S1), while spondylolysis wears a collar (scottish terrier with collar sign, m/c L5).

units.title: Meyerding Classification
units.guide: Meyerding grades by percentage of slip: I 0-25%, II 26-50%, III 51-75%, IV 76-100%, and V beyond 100% — that is spondyloptosis.

units.title: Spondylolisthesis: Features & Spondylo- Terms
units.guide: Back pain radiates to the lower limbs and palpation reveals the step sign — step off over the spinous process. Don't mix the -lo- words: spondylosis = degeneration (elderly), spondylitis = inflammation (AS), and spondyloptosis wears the inverted Napoleon hat sign.

units.title: Ankylosing Spondylitis
units.guide: AS is autoimmune: males > females, young, HLA-B27 (+), RF (-), with enthesopathy as the pathology. Sacroiliitis is the hallmark, morning stiffness improves with activity, and anterior uveitis is the classic association. On X-ray: bamboo spine (vertical syndesmophyte fusion) plus trolley track and dagger signs from ligament calcification.

units.title: DISH & OPLL
units.guide: DISH (Forestier disease) ossifies the anterior longitudinal ligament in the elderly. OPLL favours the cervical spine, also in the elderly — DISH is front, OPLL is back.

units.title: Scoliosis: Definition & Curvatures
units.guide: Scoliosis is lateral deviation of the spine by more than 10° from the central axis. The primary curvature is the largest curve; secondary curvatures are the smaller compensatory curves above and below it.

units.title: Scoliosis: Types & Adam's Test
units.guide: Spinal column deviation can be lateral, sagittal (forward bending) or rotational. Structural scoliosis is fixed and persists on bending forward; non-structural (postural/compensatory) has no rotational component and disappears on Adam's forward bending test — the screening test that separates the two.

units.title: Structural Scoliosis: Classification
units.guide: Idiopathic (m/c, no visible anomaly) splits into infantile, juvenile and adolescent (m/c). Congenital scoliosis shows a visible anomaly → deformity with wedge, hemi, unsegmented bar or block vertebrae; neuromuscular is the third category.

units.title: Scoliosis: Features & Cobb's Angle
units.guide: Shoulder asymmetry, a laterally deviated spine and the rib hump of rotational abnormality; the deformity crowds the ribs and compresses thoracic and abdominal structures. Severity is measured by Cobb's angle between the abnormal vertebrae at both ends of the primary curvature.

units.title: Risser Sign & Prognosis
units.guide: The Risser sign gauges progression potential (proportional to growth potential — high in children, low in adults) and skeletal maturity by fusion of the iliac apophysysis with the iliac crest: grades 1-4 are 25/50/75/100% lateral ossification and grade 5 is complete fusion with the ilium.

units.title: Scoliosis: Treatment
units.guide: Treatment hinges on severity & prognosis: low Cobb's + high Risser → braces (Milwaukee = cervical-thoraco-lumbo-sacral, Boston = thoraco-lumbo-sacral, Charleston); high Cobb's + low Risser → pedicle screw fixation with Harrington rods engaging all 3 spinal columns. Incidence is females > males, but prognosis is males > females.
